      "confidence": 0.95,

      "explanation": "The importer catches every `Exception`, rolls back, logs only `str(error)`, and continues.       "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/documents/cord_import.py",
      "line": 195,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Fail the import for dataset-wide or infrastructure errors, and surface the collected row errors through a nonzero CLI result."
    ,
      "title": "Import failures are silently swallowed"
    }

      "category": "correctness",
      "confidence": 0.94,
      "end_line": 34,
      "explanation": "Duplicate detection uses only the SHA-256 of the bytes.       "file": "backend/src/fieldwise/documents/service.py",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium"
    ,
      "suggestion": "Check duplicate identity using the requested `external_id` as well as content hash, and only reuse a row when the split/source identity matches."
    ,
      "title": "Content deduplication conflates dataset identities"
    }

    {

      "confidence": 0.93,
      "end_line": 55,
      "explanation": "`upsert_schema` compares the new authored object directly with the JSONB value loaded from the database. Equivalent schemas with different JSON key ordering or whitespace are treated as changed and receive a new version, defeating the documented idempotent behavior.",

      "suggestion": "Compare canonical JSON representations or the compiled schema rather than raw object equality."

  "summary": "This change adds PostgreSQL/Alembic persistence, document rendering and storage, CORD receipt ingestion, built-in receipt schemas, CLI commands, and related tests. The main risks are that rendered pages are not actually returned from the renderer, importer failures and identity handling can produce silent data loss, and schema/deduplication logic is not idempotent under common equivalent inputs."
